assumptions: Frame: heliocentric ICRF/J2000 axes, Sun centre (as idea 39 and Aster); time TDB seconds past J2000, UTC = TDB - 69.184 s, UT1 = UTC.

Forces: the Sun (GM 132712440018000000000, Aster), the Earth (GM 398600441800000, Aster; J2 0.00108262539 about the ICRF z axis, DE440), the Moon and Mercury..Neptune system barycentres (DE440 GMs), the Sun's Schwarzschild term (c 299792458 m/s); planets by Chebyshev fits of JPL Horizons (Aster's daily file and fetched records); no asteroid perturbers, no non-gravitational forces on the target.
Integrator: Dormand-Prince 5(4), relative tolerance 1e-12; the state transition matrix integrated from the point-mass gravity gradient (J2, relativity and sunlight left out of it).

Navigation: linear covariance analysis; Doppler every 2 h of a pass, one range point per pass, Delta-DOR on two baselines; stations turned by the Earth rotation angle only; light time ignored; data cut off 3 days before each TCM.
TCMs: impulsive, fixed-time position targeting of the arrival; statistics from 4000 seeded samples of N(deterministic, G P G^T); execution errors by Gates' model.

assumptions: Frame: heliocentric ICRF/J2000 axes (ideas 39 and 40); time TDB seconds past J2000, UTC = TDB - 69.184 s, UT1 = UTC; stations ITRF93 (810-005 301) turned by the Earth rotation angle only (idea 40).
Light time: Newtonian down-leg, iterated, received at the Earth's centre (JPL Horizons' definition); no Shapiro delay; the round trip is an up-leg then a down-leg.
Each day: the complex with the highest culmination takes one pass of up to 8 h centred on it, above 10 deg; its rate is the best that closes with 3 dB at the pass's lowest elevation; 3 passes a week.

DSN: 810-005 104 Rev. Q / 101 Rev. I Appendix A gain and noise, weather CD 0.9; Sun noise 105 Rev. E eqs. (10)-(11); scintillation 106 Rev. B eq. (7) on the ray's equivalent elongation, blackout at m >= 0.3.

Radio: Dawn (asteroids Vesta and Ceres) (DESCANSO article 13); required Pt/No published for 1 of its 7 rates, the rest computed from its required Eb/No, losses and modulation index; residual carrier needs a loop SNR of 10 dB.

assumptions: Frame: asteroid-centred ICRF/J2000 axes, not rotating; the asteroid on a conic about the Sun (idea 39's propagate()) from idea 40's arrival state; SAM angles as AAS 19-035 defines them. Time TDB s past J2000, UTC = TDB - 69.184 s.

Forces: the asteroid as a point mass (GM 2.68 m^3/s^2), the Sun's tide exact, sunlight on an absorber of 0.0123275681 m^2/kg (cr 1) cut off in a cylindrical shadow; no planets, no asteroid shape or spin.

Burns impulsive for targeting; main engine (450 N) above 1 m/s, small thrusters (21 N) below; one specific impulse (294.200712 s) for all; no settling burns, no execution errors, no navigation errors.

The incoming arc is flown without the asteroid's pull; the first burn is where it reaches 175000 km; waypoints from AAS 19-035 Table 1 (OSIRIS-REx at Bennu, AAM-2a waived as flown) at the same days after AAM-1.
Station-keeping holds a point fixed in the rotating SAM frame; its cost is the control acceleration's size per day; the deadband is a sphere of diameter 1000 m.
